meta.task: Club Manager season one Champions League field: reconcile the real 2025-26 final league tables from two independent source families and map every verified club to the exact Club Manager name string.
meta.rule: A position is verified only when source family A (official league or UEFA data) and source family B (press and stats sites) name the same club. Where one family was missing a position, a third independent source fetched on 2026-09-15 settled it. positionsNeeded = game Champions League places + 3 (the uclQualifiersFrom fill rule reads the next placed clubs).
meta.gameNameSource: REAL_LEAGUES in src/lib/clubManager.ts (league clubs arrays, lines 2295 to 2432) and the CM_ROSTERS keys in src/data/clubManagerRosters.ts. Every mapped name was checked by scratchpad/cm-tables/checknames.mjs to be an exact member of that league's clubs array and an exact roster key.
meta.placesSource: EURO_SLOTS at src/lib/clubManager.ts:9527, read by uclPlacesIn at :9582

uclHolder.detail: Final 30 May 2026, Puskas Arena, Budapest: 1-1 after extra time, PSG won on penalties. Shoot-out score 4-3 in the UEFA match API and ESPN; one WebFetch summary of the UEFA report said 4-2, so the shoot-out score is not shipped. Winner and runner-up agree in every source.
uclHolder.nameTrap: The game string is 'PSG' (ligue1 clubs at clubManager.ts:2321, CLUBS at :2170, roster key at clubManagerRosters.ts:3011). 'Paris Saint-Germain' is not a club string anywhere in REAL_LEAGUES; it only appears folded in CLUB_NAME_ALIASES (:3606), which guards custom club names and is not a lookup map. Second trap: the historic era2015 continental field (clubManager.ts:8390) spells it 'Paris Saint-Germain'; that is an era pool, not the modern 2026-27 world, so the modern fix must use 'PSG'. PSG also qualified as Ligue 1 champions, so the holders' route adds no extra club for 2026-27.

leagues.deductions: None mentioned. Points are play-off totals after the regular season halving (regular season: Union SG 66, Club Brugge 63, Sint-Truiden 57), not season totals; played 40 = 30 regular plus 10 play-off.
leagues.splitNote: 30 regular season games, then points halved into the Champions' Play-offs (6 clubs) and Europe Play-offs (6 clubs), 10 more games. Union SG led the regular season; Club Brugge won the Champions' Play-offs and the title. Positions 1 to 6 are the Champions' Play-off order. Every source read prints the Europe Play-off as a separate group table, not as overall places 7 to 12, so those are recorded as group order only and not shipped as positions (none is needed by the game).
leagues.uclQualifiersReal: Club Brugge (champions), league phase; Union SG (2nd) entered the third qualifying round, league path, and lost to Bodo/Glimt. The game's 1 place is the champion.
leagues.disagreements: Family A was partial (Pro League champion article gave 1 Club Brugge, 2 Union SG, 3 STVV, no points). Position 4 and all points came only from B, so a third independent source was fetched: Voetbalexpress's final Champions Play-off table (10 matchdays) names 1 Club Brugge 57, 2 Union Sint-Gillis 53, 3 Sint-Truiden VV 43, 4 RSC Anderlecht 33, 5 AA Gent 29, 6 KV Mechelen 29, matching B exactly, and the Wikipedia season page agrees. Its Europe Play-off page (Genk 38, Standard 37, Charleroi 34, Westerlo 33) also matches B. Trap: game strings are 'Union Saint-Gilloise' (not Union SG or Union St.-Gilloise), 'Sint-Truiden' (not STVV or Sint-Truidense), 'Club Brugge' (not Club Brugge KV), 'Gent' (not KAA Gent).

whatTheGameWouldDerive: With these tables, uclQualifiersFrom's rule (top uclPlacesIn per league, then the holder, then fill by depth) gives 31 league places (4+4+4+4+3+2+2+1*8) with PSG already in as Ligue 1 champions, so one fill place goes to the first deep league alphabetically: bundesliga position 5, Hoffenheim. This is arithmetic on the rule as written at clubManager.ts:9074 to :9128, not a claim about the real 2026-27 field.
